//: One number per fli check rule id — the count that may never rise. Absent = 0 = clean. `fli check --update` locks in an improvement and cannot raise; `fli check --adopt` records what is there, which is the verb for taking debt on. The findings still print either way.
//capability-ladder: All three are the exemption FJS-D146 names when it mandates this very check: a deliberately high floor under a grid. Server and Environment carry @@capabilities and @@gate(2.4.4.5), Variable @@gate(2.4.4.4), and the failure the rule warns about needs a role that HOLDS a grant and sits BELOW the write level. Basecamp has none, and it is measured rather than argued: api/src/core/gate.ts maps viewer and billing to 2 and developer to 4, and api/src/core/capabilities.ts grants viewer [] and billing [] on all three models - every grant is held at 4 or above, which is where the gate writes. So no grant is unreachable; the grid narrows WITHIN developers and admins, which is what the ladder cannot say. Flattening to @@gate(2) would make the hand-stamped grant table the only thing between a viewer and Server.delete, and seven writers stamp it. This is undecidable for fli check rather than merely unstated: the two maps are app source with no declared shape, so a rule reading them would be guessing at two module layouts. The number is 3, so a FOURTH @@capabilities model fails - and the two role sets are named here so a role gaining a grant below level 4 makes this entry visibly false in the diff.
//css-class-collision: Adopted when CI first graded the rule (FJS-D1009), and each is a rename, not a defence: .topbar, .cluster and .sidebar in routes/_module.mesa, .cluster in routes/workbench/index.mesa, .field in routes/registers/decide/index.mesa. Each takes the kit's rules as well as its own, so a kit change restyles the shell. A ceiling that falls as they are renamed.
//css-raw-literal: Adopted when CI first graded the rule (FJS-D1009): 33 raw sizes in <style> blocks, none a color — 17 in routes/workbench/index.mesa, 8 in routes/registers/index.mesa, 6 in routes/registers/decide/index.mesa, one each in components/ActionQueue.mesa and routes/_module.mesa. Most are track widths and hairlines the kit has no token for yet. Debt, not a defence; a ceiling that falls as they move onto tokens.
//detail-read-dead: Four are `portal.get()` — web/src/routes/portal/[id], web/src/components/widgets/ServiceHealthBody, git-activity and observability. It is not a row: it builds an entry from an adapter ping, over no model, so there is no node to watch and no announcement will ever arrive. Two are services that declare no channel, so nothing written elsewhere reaches their store and a watch would see what the read sees: admin/workspace's `workspaces.get` (Workspace) and settings' `users.get('me')` (User, addressed as `me`, which no node is keyed by). The other record views on this app watch, composed where the service answers more than the row (FJS-533).
//package-model-drift: One is `model Notification` against @frontierjs/notifications: EVERY id in this app is a uuid, so `id` is String where the package writes Int — and `subjectType` is a NotificationContext enum here rather than a free String, which the rule does not flag. Two are `model User` against @frontierjs/auth: `email` and `accountId` are writable at `auth().isSystemAdmin` where auth writes `auth().isAdmin`, because this app has no app-wide admin (a level is per WORKSPACE, `isAdmin` is never on its principal) and moving a person between organizations is the hub's act — CLAUDE.md § What bites here, `User`. The number is 3, so a column either package's own code starts writing differently fails.
//polymorphic-subject: AuditEvent.subjectType is the SERVICE name (api/src/core/hooks.ts), so the set grows with every service and an enum would refuse the first row a new service writes. The other four pairs in this schema are enums; this one is the exemption the rule names.

allow.service-as-system:api/src/domain/api-key: Correct: it reads what DECIDES the caller's access, the class core/hooks.ts § Why it is here and not at the Data boundary names. ApiKey carries a workspaceId, and this hook reads the key's record to answer whether the key may act at all; through a client already scoped by that answer it could find nothing and refuse every API key as unrecorded. FJS-519's own scope names this class out.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/domain/job/job: Correct: neither site is inside a call. restoreSchedules(app) runs at BOOT, since neither registry survives a restart (FJS-327), and re-registers every tenant's scheduled jobs, so the read is fleet-wide on purpose; fireBackup(app) runs when the fleet queue's schedule fires and reads the singleton HubConfig row. $ throws by name outside a call scope.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/domain/host/re: Correct: heartbeatGraceMs reads the singleton HubConfig row and is imported by jobs/server-reachability.job.ts alone, a cron with no caller. The setting is the installation's; who is asking cannot change what the timeout is.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/domain/host/en: Correct: an operator script fli runs by path, with its own createBasecampDb() and no app, no request and no principal. Nothing imports it.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/domain/notific: Correct: a sender reads the RECIPIENT's rows. NotificationPreference is @@gate(1) with userId == auth().id, so no caller's client can read another person's, and workspaceMembers lists the members of the workspaceId it is handed. It runs from jobs and hooks alike, and the file states the bypass at each site.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/domain/release: Correct: a release's steps are written for the run, not the caller. deployments.service.ts hands startRelease, recordStep, finishRelease and pushRow only a row deployInScope read through db(), the caller's own client, so the id that reaches the system client was graded first; the jobs that also call it have no caller.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/domain/site/si: Correct: the elevation runs in the publish job alone; drafts.service.ts imports PUBLISH_STEPS and a type. The appId the job carries was dispatched from drafts.publish after grantedSite() read the caller's AppEditor grant through db().

Correct: askDraft runs only from jobs/site-ask.job.ts. The appId it is handed was queued by drafts.ask after grantedSite() read the caller's AppEditor grant through db(); the functions the service imports do not elevate.

Correct: cloudflareFor and buildDraftPreview run only from jobs/site-preview.job.ts and site-publish. Every preview is queued by a drafts method holding site.id from grantedSite(), which read the caller's AppEditor grant through db(); the functions the service and app.ts import do not elevate.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/domain/backup/: Correct: Backup rows are this installation's own archives. backups.service.ts runs behind requireSystemAdmin() like /hub, rescan carries gate SYSADMIN, and remove reads the row through db() before deleteArchive; the other caller is jobs/backup-run.job.ts, which has no caller.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/services/edge/: syncStep's caller-less branch (the `domain:dns` job a machine moving enqueues, `pushAppsOn`) has no principal to read the Domain through, and the Domain's own row names the workspace it then pins into $.locals.workspaceId. A caller's branch reads through db(), scoped to ws().
allow.service-as-system:api/src/services/hub/h: Correct, and does not expire. `/hub/` is the cross-workspace tier — a separate service taking no workspace, behind one `requireSystemAdmin` hook — so reaching every tenant is the whole of what it is for. The request's own client would scope it to the sysadmin's own workspace and answer an empty fleet with a 200.
allow.service-as-system:api/src/services/metri: MetricSeries, MetricPoint and MetricHour are @@gate(8) in junction's db/metrics.lite and carry no workspace column: host-wide rows, read only behind this service's SYSADMIN gate, the tier hub.service.ts is.
allow.test-port-literal:web/test/verify-screen: 8443 and 8080 are the `port` column of a Domain and an App the drive types into a form -- data a container publishes, never a port the drive binds or reaches.

allow.test-port-literal:api/test/verify-dns.mj: 7129 is the App.port of an nginx container the drive records and never starts.
baseUrl on a HubConfig row; the sweep under test reads heartbeats and never connects to it.
allow.test-port-literal:api/test/edge.test.ts: 8443 is a Domain.port patched on a row; nothing binds it.
allow.test-port-literal:api/test/rollback.test: 8080 is the App.port snapshotted into a Release and compared back; nothing binds it.
